thesis: Dominari Holdings is a micro-cap financial holding company built around wealth management, broker-dealer, investment banking, and asset management subsidiaries. Revenue grew roughly 487% in FY2025 to $$123.1M, but the company is still loss-making on a GAAP basis and carries an accumulated deficit of about $325M. The stock trades at a low single-digit price, below both 50-day and 200-day moving averages, with minimal analyst coverage and no real options market. This is a speculative turnaround / restructuring story with a heavily dilution-prone capital structure and a recent dividend track record. It is suitable only for highly risk-tolerant capital.

drivers: Wealth management and broker-dealer subsidiaries continue scaling; FY2026 revenue approaches $180–$200M with improved operating leverage
Asset management and sales & trading segments generate consistent quarterly profitability, validating the holding-company model
Strategic asset sales (e.g., American Bitcoin Corp stake) and special dividends sustain investor interest and provide cash flexibility
Drone/defense advisory contracts (Powerus/Tandem) evolve into a recurring revenue stream or spin-off event
Market re-rates the stock to 1.0–1.2x book value or a modest forward revenue multiple on 10–12M shares

base_case.assumptions: Revenue grows 50% in FY2026 to ~$185M, with operating losses narrowing but GAAP net income still negative or break-even due to stock-based compensation and acquisition integration. The stock continues to trade around current price-to-book (~1.75x) and a low enterprise-value-to-revenue multiple as investors wait for sustained profitability. The base case implies a slow grind higher with high volatility, capped by the micro-cap float and ongoing capital needs.

risks: Revenue growth stalls as legacy pharmaceutical licensing revenue (AIkido era) fades faster than financial services revenue scales
Ongoing GAAP losses burn the $27.5M cash balance within 12–18 months, forcing dilutive equity raises at depressed prices
Stock compensation and convertible instruments continue to dilute shareholders; accumulated deficit keeps expanding
Special dividends are suspended, removing the main catalyst that has attracted retail/speculative interest
Weak liquidity and no options market make exit difficult during a risk-off rotation or broad small-cap selloff

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings release and management update on revenue mix and segment profitability
Potential additional special dividend announcements or strategic asset monetization updates
Drone/defense advisory contract milestones (Powerus/Tandem) and any new M&A or spin-off updates
Annual 10-K filing showing FY2026 full-year revenue, net loss, and audited segment breakdown

key_risks: Micro-cap float (7.7M shares) and low average daily volume make the stock illiquid and prone to sharp moves
GAAP losses and accumulated deficit of ~$325M; path to sustainable profitability is unproven
Capital structure includes preferred stock, convertible notes, and warrants that can dilute common shareholders
Limited analyst coverage, no options market, and minimal institutional ownership reduce price discovery
Dependence on market/trading activity and M&A fee revenue makes results cyclical
Special dividends are non-recurring and may not continue; the recent yield has been a return of capital rather than earnings-based
